gemma4_verdict: google/gemma-4-31B-it (dense) fits on 32 GB with one important caveat: its weights are modest but its KV/SWA memory machinery is the dominant constraint. At 4-bit the WEIGHTS land at ~17-20 GB (Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL GGUF ~18-18.8 GB; QAT GGUF reports ~18 GB total for model + modest context; AWQ/compressed-tensors int4 ~17-20 GB). Q5_K_M is roughly ~22-23 GB and Q6_K ~26-27 GB of weights (extrapolated from the 31B param count; exact 31B GGUF sizes vary by uploader). The decisive factor is the hybrid sliding-window attention: 60 layers = 50 local (SWA) + 10 full/global. The GLOBAL layers are expensive (community/vLLM figures: ~1 GiB per global layer, ~16 MiB per local layer; ~15.7 GiB per sequence at 256K bf16), but the project's stated '~3.6 GB fixed SWA KV cache' is real and specific: in llama.cpp the default SWA KV checkpoint size is ~3,600 MiB (~3.6 GB) each, and the default checkpoint count is high (32), which is what produces the notorious 'Gemma 4 31B context VRAM is insane' reports (115+ GB if left at defaults). With -np 1 (single SWA reservation) plus KV quantization this collapses to a usable footprint. Measured: UD-Q4_K_XL with FP16 KV used ~22.3 GB at 16,384 context; with Q8_0 KV that drops to roughly model + ~3-4 GB; with Q4_0 KV even 256K fits in ~9.7 GB of cache. So Gemma 4 31B at UD-Q4_K_XL + Q8_0 KV cache + -np 1 fits 16k context comfortably inside 32 GB. CRITICAL nuance for quant selection: Unsloth ships ONLY a single QAT GGUF (UD-Q4_K_XL) for Gemma 4 because Google's quantization-aware training means precisions HIGHER than that QAT-Q4 do not improve and can DEGRADE accuracy — so for Gemma 4 the usual 'go to Q5/Q6 for quality' logic is inverted: the QAT UD-Q4_K_XL is the quality sweet spot, not a compromise. Naive q4_0 from QAT loses accuracy (e.g. 70.2% top-1 on 26B-A4B) which Unsloth's dynamic method recovers to ~85.6%.
qwen3_verdict: Qwen/Qwen3-32B (dense, text-only, 64 layers, GQA with 8 KV heads, head_dim 128) is the more conventional and predictable fit. GGUF weight sizes (bartowski/Unsloth/official, sizes mirror the same-architecture QwQ-32B reference): Q4_K_M ~19.9 GB, Q5_K_M ~23.3 GB, Q6_K ~26.9 GB, Q8_0 ~34.8 GB. Its KV cache scales cleanly and predictably with GQA (no fixed SWA block): at FP16 ~4.0 GB at 16k and ~8.0 GB at 32k; Q8 KV halves that (~2.0 GB / ~4.0 GB at 16k/32k) and Q4 KV quarters it. Fit math on 32 GB: Q4_K_M (~19.9 GB) + 16k FP16 KV (~4 GB) = ~24 GB, leaving headroom -> fits easily, and even 32k FP16 (~28 GB) fits. Q5_K_M (~23.3 GB) + 16k Q8 KV (~2 GB) = ~25 GB -> fits with room for 16k+; Q5_K_M + 16k FP16 KV (~4 GB) = ~27 GB -> still fits. Q6_K (~26.9 GB) + 16k Q8 KV (~2 GB) = ~29 GB -> fits but TIGHT, little margin for the co-resident embedder/reranker. Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL dynamic quants are available for the Qwen3 line and measurably beat plain Q4_K_M at similar/smaller size (the dynamic method puts important matrices at Q5_K). Because Qwen3-32B has no fixed-cost SWA block and a textbook GQA KV curve, it is the easier model to reason about and to co-resident with helper models inside 32 GB.
benchmarks: Quantization quality benchmarks (not task-capability benchmarks): llama.cpp official 7B perplexity penalties — Q4_K_M +0.0535 ppl, Q5_K_S +0.0353 ppl, Q6_K near-lossless (between Q5_K_M and Q8_0), Q8_0 ~0.000, Q3_K_M +0.2437 ppl, Q2_K +0.8698 ppl. Relative quant error is SMALLER on 32B than on 7B (more params -> each weight matters less), so Q4_K_M is even more competitive at this scale. Unsloth Dynamic 2.0: UD-Q4_K_XL achieved 99.9% KL-divergence retention (SOTA on the Pareto frontier) and on Aider Polyglot scored 60.9% vs 61.8% bf16 (~1.5% relative gap) for the 480B-A35B coder model — i.e. near-full quality at Q4. Unsloth Qwen3.5 GGUF benchmark: Q4_K_M ppl 6.6097 vs Q5_K_M 6.5828 (a 0.027 gap, negligible for writing, marginally relevant for long math reasoning). KLD (not perplexity) is the gold standard per the 'Accuracy is Not All You Need' paper; perplexity can overfit calibration data. Gemma 4 QAT: naive Q4_0 from QAT = 70.2% top-1 (26B-A4B) recovered to 85.6% by Unsloth dynamic method.
factual_accuracy: Quantization-induced factual degradation is negligible for both models at Q4_K_M and above for writing/synthesis tasks; the gold-standard metric (KL divergence vs bf16) is ~99.9% retained for Unsloth dynamic Q4. Where quant DOES erode reliability is long multi-step reasoning/math chains, where a small early token-probability shift can route to a wrong step (Q4 ppl 6.61 vs Q5 6.58 on Qwen3.5 corresponds to measurably lower MATH/GSM8K accuracy). For Labmate's academic-writing and citation-faithfulness needs, that reasoning-chain sensitivity is the only quant-driven accuracy concern; choosing Q5_K_M (Qwen3) or staying on the QAT UD-Q4_K_XL (Gemma 4) mitigates it. The dominant non-quant risk is the Gemma 4 SWA/KV checkpoint misconfiguration producing OOM or (on some ROCm builds) token corruption — a deployment failure, not a model hallucination.
inference_speed: Quant choice has a secondary speed effect relevant to VRAM fit: higher quant = larger weights = more memory-bandwidth traffic per token, so Q4_K_M decodes faster than Q6_K on the same dense 32B (both are bandwidth-bound). imatrix-calibrated dynamic quants cost ~5-10% slower inference vs plain quants for their accuracy gain. KV-cache quantization (Q8_0 or Q4_0 KV via --cache-type-k/--cache-type-v) is the key lever that lets you keep a higher WEIGHT quant on 32 GB without losing context, at near-zero speed cost; on llama.cpp a good asymmetric setting is K=q4_0, V=q8_0. Flash attention (rocWMMA on RDNA3+, Metal) reduces KV memory AND speeds up with zero quality loss. [uncertain] No source gives tok/s split by quant level for these two specific models on a 32 GB card; the speed ranking is inferred from bandwidth-bound behavior.
multimodal_support: Memory-relevant note: Gemma 4 31B's multimodal (image) path requires loading the separate mmproj vision projector in addition to the language weights, adding to VRAM pressure on a 32 GB card — budget extra headroom (the projector is small but non-zero and the vision tower activations add transient memory). Qwen3-32B base is text-only, so it carries no extra multimodal VRAM cost (its KV math above is the whole story). For a 32 GB co-residency budget, the text-only Qwen3-32B is easier to fit alongside the embedder + reranker; if Gemma 4's vision is required, the mmproj plus the fixed SWA block make the budget noticeably tighter. [uncertain] Exact mmproj VRAM for Gemma 4 31B on a 32 GB card not separately measured in sources.
context_window: Both advertise 256K-262K nominal. The 32 GB VRAM-fit question is really 'how much context fits with weights + helpers resident'. Qwen3-32B (clean GQA): Q4_K_M leaves room for 32k+ FP16 KV inside 32 GB; Q5_K_M + Q8 KV comfortably holds 16k-32k. Gemma 4 31B: WITHOUT KV quantization and with default SWA checkpoints it blows past 32 GB even at 8k-16k (the ~3.6 GB-per-checkpoint x32 default = the 'insane VRAM' reports); WITH -np 1 + Q8_0/Q4_0 KV quantization it holds 16k easily and 256K is feasible at Q4_0 KV (~9.7 GB cache). So both meet the project's '16k+ context KV cache' bar on 32 GB, but Gemma 4 only after correct SWA/KV configuration, whereas Qwen3-32B meets it out of the box. The project's stated '~3.6 GB fixed SWA KV cache' for Gemma 4 corresponds to the per-checkpoint size; the practical fixed cost with -np 1 is roughly one such block plus the 10 global layers' cache.
non_cuda_support: GGUF quants enabling these VRAM profiles are available and working on non-CUDA backends for both. Gemma 4 31B: Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL and QAT UD-Q4_K_XL GGUFs (llama.cpp/Ollama/LM Studio on ROCm, Vulkan, Metal); on some ROCm/HIP builds certain Gemma 4 GGUF quants emit garbage tokens (use ggml-org/known-good quant or the Vulkan backend). Gemma 4's SWA flash-attention path had a llama.cpp CUDA illegal-memory-access bug after the 2nd SWA checkpoint that also stresses non-CUDA builds; ensure an up-to-date llama.cpp (the 2026 fix cut context-heavy memory ~40%). Qwen3-32B: GGUF quants are mature on ROCm and Metal (Unsloth, bartowski, official) with no SWA-specific pitfalls. Note FP8 KV-cache quantization is weak/absent on consumer RDNA3, so on AMD use Q8_0/Q4_0 GGUF KV quant instead to hit the context budgets above. On Apple unified memory, the same weight+KV math applies but the 48 GB tier removes most of the 32 GB tightness for either model.
over_refusal_risk: Not applicable to the VRAM/quantization dimension — refusal behavior is model policy and is unchanged by quant level or VRAM fit.
ecosystem_toolchain: Quant/VRAM tooling maturity: Unsloth Dynamic 2.0 GGUFs (UD-Q4_K_XL etc.) cover both model lines and are the recommended quality-per-byte choice (imatrix-calibrated, 150+ KLD benchmarks). For Gemma 4 specifically, Unsloth ships a SINGLE QAT GGUF (UD-Q4_K_XL) by design — there is no higher-quant ladder to climb because QAT makes higher precision non-beneficial; this simplifies selection but means 'use Q5/Q6 for more quality' is NOT a Gemma 4 option. For Qwen3-32B the full ladder (Q4_K_M / Q5_K_M / Q6_K / Q8_0 plus UD-Q4_K_XL) exists from bartowski, Unsloth, and Qwen official. KV-cache quantization is exposed in llama.cpp (--cache-type-k/-v), Ollama, and LM Studio; vLLM supports FP8 KV on CUDA/Instinct. LM Studio surfaced the Gemma 4 KV-footprint problem (bug tracker #1740); fixes and -np 1 guidance are documented in llama.cpp discussions.
labmate_relevance: HIGH. Labmate's entire deployment premise (CLAUDE.md) is a single 32 GB GPU host running a Gemma 4 31B orchestrator and a 32B specialist via vLLM. Whether each model fits at a quant that retains academic-writing quality, with 16k+ context KV cache, AND optionally the bge embedder + reranker co-resident, directly determines the serving topology (one model at a time vs co-resident, swap strategy, chosen quant flags). The Gemma 4 SWA/KV fixed-cost behavior is a concrete operational landmine that must be configured correctly (-np 1, KV quant) or the orchestrator will OOM.
recommendation: Co-residency budget on 32 GB: bge-small-en-v1.5 (~33M params, ~0.13 GB FP16; cited 0.13 GB) + bge-reranker-v2-m3 (~568M params, ~1.1 GB FP16 weights, ~2.3 GB with runtime/activation overhead as the project cites) together cost ~2.4-2.5 GB resident. That is affordable ALONGSIDE a single Q4 32B model + 16k KV, but NOT alongside a Q6_K 32B (Q6_K ~27 GB + 2 GB KV + 2.4 GB helpers > 32 GB). Concrete guidance: (1) Qwen3-32B sweet spot for 32 GB WITH helpers co-resident = Q4_K_M or UD-Q4_K_XL (~20 GB) + Q8_0 KV at 16k (~2 GB) + bge pair (~2.4 GB) = ~24-25 GB, leaving margin; if you want Q5_K_M for max writing fidelity, drop the reranker to CPU/on-demand (Q5_K_M ~23.3 GB + ~2 GB KV = ~25 GB leaves little for both helpers). (2) Gemma 4 31B: use the QAT UD-Q4_K_XL (the quality sweet spot by design) + -np 1 + Q8_0 KV; this fits 16k context in ~22-24 GB and leaves room for the bge pair — there is NO Q5/Q6 Gemma 4 option to consider, which actually simplifies the decision. (3) The general 'Q5/Q6 sweet spot retaining near-full academic-writing quality' question: for Qwen3-32B, Q5_K_M is the textbook sweet spot and fits 32 GB (with KV quant) — but for WRITING specifically the Q4->Q6 quality delta is negligible, so Q4_K_M/UD-Q4_K_XL is the pragmatic best value and the only choice that comfortably co-resides with both helper models; reserve Q5_K_M for runs where long multi-step reasoning/math fidelity matters and you can shed a helper. For Gemma 4, the QAT UD-Q4_K_XL IS the sweet spot. Bottom line for Labmate: both models fit 32 GB with 16k+ context and the bge pair at Q4; Qwen3-32B wins this dimension because its KV scaling is predictable, it has no fixed SWA cost, and it offers a real Q5_K_M step-up if needed — whereas Gemma 4 fits only after careful SWA/KV configuration and is locked to its QAT Q4.
